children: Norway's annual core inflation rate eased more than expected in October, Statistics Norway (SSB) data showed on Tuesday, reducing pressure on Norges Bank to raise interest rates.
Core inflation, which strips out changing energy prices and taxes, stood at 2.7% year-on-year, down from 3.0% in September, and below the 2.8% expected by analysts in a Reuters poll.
Norges Bank had expected core inflation of 2.7%.
Norway's currency, the crown, weakened to 10.55 against the euro
by 0703 GMT, from 10.54 ahead of the data release.
Norway's central bank last week kept its policy interest rate on hold at 4.50% and reiterated that it may still tighten policy to contain consumer prices.

Norges Bank Governor Ida Wolden Bache said at the time that it will likely be necessary to keep the policy rate elevated for a time and that the board was prepared to raise the policy rate if needed to bring inflation down within a reasonable time.
Norges Bank, which targets core inflation of 2.0%, is scheduled to make its next policy rate announcement on December 17.
